component.name: Cheat Engine for Linux
component.summary: Memory scanner, debugger, and injector for modding games and apps

description.p: A Linux-native reimplementation of Cheat Engine in C++ and Qt6: memory scanning, pointer scanning, an auto-assembler, an interactive multi-thread debugger, structure dissection, cheat tables, and Lua scripting.
Focused on single-player game modding and reverse engineering. It does not target multiplayer anti-cheat.
Compatibility work across native, Wine and Proton, ARM64, ARM32, x32, RISC-V, s390x and PowerPC guests, .NET, Mono and emulator targets, with explicit errors where a feature is not supported.
Site-specific auto-assembler injection templates, consistent typed memory operations across the GUI, CLI, and Lua, and extensive correctness fixes for scanning, debugging, parsing, and scripting.
Improved GUI layouts, light and dark themes, scrolling, process selection, live settings, and large form canvases.
Correctness, safety and portability fixes.
Cheat Engine parity sweep: global symbols, code pages and broader Lua support.
Emulator and sandboxed targets, obfuscated values, and scriptable find what writes.
Find what writes and code injection on Wine and Proton.
Whole-application interface overhaul and a deeper IL2CPP dissector.
Scanner performance overhaul.
Mono and Unity dissector, diagnostics, Lua table compatibility and debugger polish.

Bug-fix release: light/dark theme applies live from Settings; the memory browser explains ptrace-permission failures instead of showing a blank pane; the .deb grants ptrace access automatically at install (setcap) and the "process not readable" dialog offers a one-click pkexec grant; the AppImage now bundles the Qt platform plugins and runs.

Full CLI / headless parity: every GUI tool is now scriptable from the terminal through the Lua API and the cescan headless runner, so features are testable without the GUI. New bindings for pointer scan, structure dissect, managed-runtime detection, find-what-writes/accesses, break-and-trace, branch mapper, register/stack read-write, find-statics, cheat-table save/load, trainer generation, ceserver connect, and address-list grouping. Also fixes a trainer code-generation bug (invalid float literal for whole-number values).

Complete interactive debugger (software + hardware breakpoints, register editing, XMM, thread switcher, memory pane, scriptable Lua debugger); cecore can act as a ceserver for remote memory access; untrusted cheat-table security hardening.
AOB-injection fix, 32-bit/WoW64/Wine support, cheat-table inline editing.
Real-time results, Cheat Engine style scanning and a hardened core.
PortProton, Lutris and Heroic support.
First tagged release.
